verse: If you have bitter envy and contentions in your hearts, do not glory and do not be liars against the truth. Such wisdom is not coming from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, and devilish. For where envy and strife are, there is disorder and every kind of evil work. (Jas 3:14-16)
Rest in the Lord and wait patiently for him; do not fret over those who prosper in their way, over those who bring evil devices to pass. (Ps 37:7)

Let nothing be done by contention, nor in vain glory. Instead, in humility, let each of you esteem others to be better than yourselves. Let every person look not to his own interests, but to the interests of others. (Phil 2:3-4)
Let not your heart envy sinners. But be in the fear of the Lord always. For surely there is a reward, and your expectations will not be cut off. (Pro 23:17-18)

Because you said, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess them,” though the Lord was there—therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, “I will do to you according to your anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred against them. And I will make myself known among you when I judge you.” (Eze 35:10-11)
As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was laid waste, so I will deal with you; you shall be laid waste. (Eze 35:15)

You should not have gloated over your brother on the day of his calamity; you should not have rejoiced over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction; you should not have spoken proudly in the day of their distress. (Obad 1:12)

You should not have entered the gate of my people on the day of their calamity; you should not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor should you have laid your hands on their goods in the day of their calamity. (Obad 1:13)

Where do wars and contentions among you come from? Is it not from this: from your own desires, which battle within your members? You desire, and you do not have. You envy and you kill, and you are unable to obtain; so, you contend and engage in disputes. You do not have, because you do not ask. (Jas 4:1-2)
But as for me, my feet were nearly moved; my steps had nearly slipped. For I was envious over the iniquitous, seeing the prosperity of the wicked. (Ps 73:2-3)
A man who hurries to become rich, and who envies others, does not know that destitution will overwhelm him. (Pro 28:22)

When I turned myself toward all the works that my hands had made, and to the labors in which I had perspired to no purpose, I saw emptiness and affliction of the soul in all things, and that nothing is permanent under the sun. (Eccl 2:11)
Do not envy the evil, neither desire to be with them; for their minds plot violence, and their lips talk of mischief. (Pro 24:1-2)
If I have been glad at the ruin of him who hated me or have exulted when evil found him – for I have not given my mouth to sin by wishing a curse upon his life. (Job 31:29-30)
Whoever enjoys the fall of the just will perish in a snare, and grief will consume them before they die. (Sir 27:29)

Do not lie in wait like the wicked against the dwelling of the righteous; do not spoil his resting place; for though a just man falls seven times, they will rise again; but the wicked shall fall into evil. (Pro 24:15-16)
Do not rejoice when your enemies fall, and do not let your heart be glad when they stumble, or else the Lord will see it and be displeased, and he turn away his wrath from them. (Pro 24:17-18)
Do not fret because of those who do evil. Do not be envious of the wicked; For the evil have no hope of things to come, and the lamp of the wicked shall be put out. (Pro 24:19-20)

He had possessions of sheep and of herds, and a very large family. Because of this, the Palestinians envied him, so, at that time, they obstructed all the wells that the servants of his father Abraham had dug, filling them with soil. (Gen 26:14-15)
He who devises to do evil will be called a wicked person. The planning of folly is sin, and the scorner is an abomination to all. (Pro 24:8-9)
Let us not become desirous of empty glory, competing with one another, envying one another. (Gal 5:26)

Then Saul became exceedingly angry, and this word was displeasing in his eyes. And he said: “They have given David ten thousand, and to me they gave only one thousand. What is left for him, except the kingdom itself?” Therefore, Saul did not regard David with a good eye, from that day and thereafter. (1 Sam 18:8-9)
For all the law is fulfilled in one statement, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” But if you bite and devour one another, take care that you are not consumed by one another. (Gal 5:14-15)
Wrath is cruel, anger is outraging, but who is able to stand before jealousy? (Pro 27:4)

The patriarchs, because of jealousy, sold Joseph into Egypt; but God was with him, and delivered him out of all his tribulations, and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who appointed him governor over Egypt and over all his house. (Acts 7:9-10)

For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, deceived, enslaved to various sinful desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. But when the goodness and kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not by works of righteousness which we had done, but according to his mercy, by the water of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit. (Tit 3:3-5)
If there is still among you envy, strife, and divisions, are you not carnal, and behaving in a human way? (1 Cor 3:3)
Therefore, you are inexcusable, whoever you are who judges others; for when you pass judgement on another you condemn yourself, because you, the judge, do the same things. (Rom 2:1)
Why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise your brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. (Rom 14:10)
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged. For with whatever judgment you judge, so shall you be judged; and with whatever measure you measure out, so shall it be measured back to you. (Matt 7:1-2)

If I have the gift of prophecy and know all mysteries, and all knowledge, and if I have all the faith, so that I could remove mountains, but If I have no love, I am nothing. If I distribute all my goods to feed the poor, and if I deliver my body to be burned, but have no love, it profits me nothing. (1 Cor 13:2-3)
Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends. (Jn 15:13)
We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love our brethren. Those who do not love abide in death. (1 Jn 3:14)
This is my commandment that you love one another, just as I have loved you. (Jn 15:12)
Now that you have purified your souls by your obedience to the truth and have come to have a sincere love for other believers, love one another earnestly with all your heart. (1 Pet 1:22)
This is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as he has commanded us. (1 Jn 3:23)
No one has seen God at any time. But if we love one another, God is abiding in us, and his love has been perfected in us. (1 Jn 4:12)
In this we have known the love of God, because he has laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for others. (1 Jn 3:16)
If then you fulfill the royal law, according to the scriptures, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself”, you do well. (Jas 2:8)
As every man has received a gift, serve one another as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. (1 Pet 4:10)

The commandments, “You shall not commit adultery; You shall not murder; You shall not steal; You shall not covet”; and if there be any other commandment, are summed up in this word, “Love your neighbor as yourself.” (Rom 13:9)
Love does no harm to a neighbor; love therefore is the fulfilling of the law. (Rom 13:10)

May the God of patience and comfort grant you to live in harmony with one another, according to Christ Jesus, so that you may with one mind and one mouth glorify God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. (Rom 15:5-6)
Receive one another, therefore, just as Christ has received us, for the glory of God. (Rom 15:7)

Now I beseech you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you speak the same thing and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be joined together in the same mind and in the same judgement. (1 Cor 1:10)
So let us not be weary in doing what is right, for in due time we will reap, if we do not give up. (Gal 6:9)

In this way, the children of God and the children of the devil are made manifest. Everyone who does not do what is right, is not of God, and anyone who does not love his brother or sister. (1 Jn 3:10)
Let mutual love continue. Do not be forgetful to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing this, some, being not aware of it, have entertained angels. (Heb 13:1-2)
Therefore, while we have the opportunity, let us do good toward everyone and especially to those who are of the household of the faith. (Gal 6:10)
Let no one seek his own advantage, but that of others. (1 Cor 10:24)
